sections.title: Output shape & calling convention
sections.intro: Plan: a new `toTypeScript(expr, options)` on Engine/Registry returning `{ code, types: Map<name, 'type X = …'> }`, plus `joinTypeScript(outputs)` that merges type maps (dedupe by name) and `renderTypeScriptFile(output)` that writes one file. Natively-TS types (string, number, boolean, Date, Map, arrays, tuples, unions) are inlined, never put in the map. Only `type` aliases, never `interface`. Tests compile the output with the `typescript` compiler, run the JS, and compare against `engine.run`.

questions.question: What is the API surface?

options.label: engine.toTypeScript + joinTypeScript + renderTypeScriptFile
options.description: Lives beside toCode/toGinCode. Output `{ code, types: Map<string,string>, prelude? }`. join merges maps; a name with two different bodies throws.

options.label: A TypeScriptExporter class you add exprs to
options.description: `const x = new TsExporter(engine); x.add('name', expr); x.file()` — accumulates types across calls itself.

options.label: Both
options.description: Free functions, plus a small accumulator built on them.

questions.why: Decides naming, docs, and how the 'joinable' requirement is met.

questions.question: gin calls take a named-args object (`x.add({other: 3})`, lambda `args.name`). How should methods and exported functions take parameters in TS?

options.label: One args object: (args: { plan: string }) => R
options.description: Mirrors gin 1:1 (optional args, defaults, generics just work); an LLM writing against the types sees exactly gin's contract. Built-in natives still compile to idiomatic TS (`a + b`, `s.toUpperCase()`).

options.label: Positional: (plan: string) => R
options.description: More idiomatic TS, but arg order must be fixed from declaration order and optional-in-the-middle gets awkward.

questions.why: Every exported type with a method, and every exported function signature, depends on it.

questions.question: gin evaluation is async (host natives can hit a DB/network). Should generated functions be async?

options.label: Always async; every host/method call is awaited
options.description: Simple and always correct. Methods on types are `(args) => Promise<R>`... or `R | Promise<R>`.

options.label: Async only where effects include EXTERNAL/SYSTEM
options.description: Pure functions stay sync and nicer; relies on effects being declared correctly by hosts.

options.label: Always sync
options.description: Host natives must be sync. Simplest output, limits real use.

questions.why: Changes every method signature in the types map and how an LLM must write code against them.

questions.question: A function's free variables (globals registered on the engine, `extras` at run) — how do they reach the compiled code?

options.label: A typed context parameter: fn(args, ctx: Ctx)
options.description: Ctx type (only the globals actually referenced) goes in the types map. Pure, testable, no ambient state; the host passes real implementations.

options.label: `declare const pi: number` in the types file
options.description: Code reads naturally (`pi`), host must provide them on globalThis or wrap in a module.

options.label: Factory: makeFns(ctx) returns the functions
options.description: Globals are closure vars; one ctx bound once for all exported functions.

questions.why: Defines what 'runnable' means — what a host does to actually call the JS.

sections.title: Natives & runtime semantics
sections.intro: gin has ~200 built-in natives (num.add, text.split, list.map, date.addMonths, color.mix, …) plus host natives registered by id (e.g. `Customer.upgrade`) and methods implemented by gin exprs.

questions.question: How do built-in natives compile?

options.label: Inline idiomatic TS + a small emitted prelude for the rest
options.description: `a + b`, `s.toUpperCase()`, `xs.map(...)` inline; non-trivial ones (date.addMonths, color.mix, epsilon num.eq, duration math) become tiny helper functions emitted once in a `prelude` (only the ones used). Output file is self-contained, no gin dependency at run.

options.label: Import a runtime from @aeye/gin (`$gin.num.add(a,b)`)
options.description: Exact parity with gin's impls, uniform, but the compiled code depends on gin and reads worse.

options.label: Inline only; unsupported natives throw at export
options.description: Smallest output; some programs won't export.

questions.why: Biggest chunk of work and decides whether output is standalone.

questions.question: gin's `num.eq` is epsilon-approximate. Compiled equality should be…

options.label: Faithful (helper with gin's epsilon)
options.description: Compiled result always matches engine.run.

options.label: Plain ===
options.description: Idiomatic; can differ from gin on float math.

questions.question: Methods on referenced types (e.g. Person.fullName implemented by a gin template expr, Customer.upgrade by a host native). In the types they are function-typed properties. Where do their implementations come from at run time?

options.label: The value already carries them; host attaches impls
options.description: `type Person = { firstName: string; fullName: () => Promise<string> }`. Compiled code just calls `p.fullName()`. For expr-implemented methods we ALSO emit a constructor/helper (`makePerson(data)`) that attaches compiled bodies, so `new Person` in a program works.

options.label: Compile methods to free functions (Person_fullName(self))
options.description: Values stay plain data (JSON-friendly); types file lists methods as functions not properties — contradicts 'methods are properties'.

questions.why: Decides how `new` of a user type and every method call compile.

questions.question: Type constraints (num{min=0, whole}, text{pattern}, list{max}) and named extensions (`Email extends text`):

options.label: Plain aliases + constraints as /** */ doc comments
options.description: `/** pattern: ^\d+$ */ type Email = string`. Docs from gin go in too, so an LLM reading the types sees them.

options.label: Branded types (string & { __brand: 'Email' })
options.description: Nominal safety, but LLM-written code needs casts everywhere.

options.label: Drop constraints entirely
Emit a structural guard per type used (`isPerson(x)`)
options.description: Only for types actually checked; lives in the prelude.

options.label: Not supported: export reports a problem
options.description: Keep v1 small.

questions.question: `flow: exit` (unwind to engine.run with a value) — compile as…

options.label: Throw a prelude ExitSignal caught by the outermost exported function
Treat like return from the exported function

questions.question: Which export options do you want in v1? (pick all)

options.label: types: 'referenced' | 'none' — emit every non-native type referenced, transitively
includeComments — gin docs as /** */
name — the exported function/const name for a top-level lambda
prelude: 'inline' | 'separate' — helpers in the code or as their own map entry
export keyword on emitted types/functions
async: 'always' | 'auto' override

questions.question: For the 'hand an LLM the types file' scenario, how far should v1 go?

options.label: Offline test only: types file compiles standalone; a hand-written function against it compiles and runs
options.description: Proves the contract without spending model calls.

options.label: Also an integration script (like npm run integration) that asks a real model to write the function, compiles and runs it
Skip it; just exprs → TS parity tests
Commit locally, I'll say when to push/release
Commit and push (tag v* publishes)
